text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Greek operatic soprano MARIA CALLAS, who was renowned for her dramatic interpretations, was born in 1923.
American soldier and politician General ALEXANDER HAIG was born in 1924.
British drummer with the 'Tremeloes' DAVID MUNDEN was born in 1943.
British bass player with 'Def Leppard' RICK SAVAGE was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1814 : The MARQUIS DE SADE died in a lunatic asylum in
Charenton. The French author was imprisoned for sexual offenses. He wrote plays and novels dealing explicitly with a variety of sexual practices, including sadism.
1859 : The radical anti-slavery campaigner JOHN BROWN was

hanged for treason against Virginia. Three years earlier BROWN and his sons murdered five pro-slavery settlers in Kansas. BROWN planned to set up a republic in the Appalachians as a base for abolitionists and runaways to fight slavery. BROWN and 21 men attacked Harpers Ferry in West Virginia and occupied the town. Federal troops led by ROBERT E. LEE recaptured the town
and charged BROWN with treason. His trial and subsequent hanging caused a greater rift between the north and south over the fate of slavery.
1928 : Britain's first 22 public telephone boxes appeared
in London.
1932 : Australia's DON BRADMAN was ruled unfit for the
first Test which opened with destructive leg-theory bowling by England's HAROLD LARWOOD and BILL VOCE.
1934 : US Olympic swimming champion JOHNNY WEISSMULLER
starred in his second film "Tarzan and His Mate".
1966 : More than 4,500 Qantas staff were laid off because
of a pilots' strike.
1971 : QUEEN ELIZABETH's allowance was almost doubled

from 475,000 pounds to 980,000 pounds. The increase was the recommendation of an all-party House of Commons select committee. Most of the increase was taken up by wages to her 375 full-time and 100 part-time staff.
1973 : Papua New Guinea achieved self-government.
1981 : A mercenary-led attempt to overthrow the left-wing

Seychelles government was thwarted before it began. The 44 mercenaries, disguised as tourists, identified themselves as members of the "Froth Blowers" club looking forward to a golfing and drinking holiday. Their real mission was discovered when one of the "golf" bags fell open at the Pointe Larue airport to reveal a gun. The group's leader was Colonel 'MAD MIKE' HOARE, notorious as a Congo mercenary in the 1960's. Upon discovery they escaped by shooting up the airport and ordering the pilot of an Air India jet to fly them to South Africa. There they were eventually charged with hijacking.
1990 : West German chancellor HELMUT KOHL won the first
all-Germany election since 1933. KOHL's Christian Democrats won more than half of the seats with the communist ex-rulers of East Germany winning a handful of seats.
